name: pr-review-workflow
description: Reviews a GitHub pull request end to end: posts inline findings, edits the branch to address them, re-reviews until clean, then merges or asks.

auto_approve.title: Auto-approve on convergence
auto_approve.description: Merge automatically once the review loop finds nothing open. When off, the plugin asks before merging.

self_start.title: Self-started reviews
self_start.description: What happens when Claude decides on its own to review a pull request. ask: you confirm first. auto: no confirmation when the pull request is ready (open, not a draft, unreviewed, checks not failing, the clone's work committed and pushed, no earlier run here); anything else still asks. A review Claude started itself never merges without asking you.

check_command.title: Check command
check_command.description: The reviewed repository's own check command. It proves suggested changes before they post, and gates each editing round: fixes must leave it passing. Leave empty to skip both.

keep_ledgers.title: Ledgers kept per repository
keep_ledgers.description: At the start of each review and after each merge, the sweep keeps this many finished finding ledgers per repository as the audit record and prunes older ones. A run whose pull request is still open is never pruned.

double_review.title: Second review pass
double_review.description: When a gap pass runs after a single-reviewer first review: off, risky (a secrets, automation, or sensitive probe fired), or always. The gap pass reads the existing findings and reports only what they miss. A sharded review always ends with one, whatever this is set to, because only a whole-diff pass sees defects that span shards.

local_standards.title: Local standards files
local_standards.description: Space-separated globs, relative to your clone, of untracked files holding the project's own rules and standards. Their substance guides every review; their names and text never reach the pull request. Leave empty for projects without them.

reviewer_model.title: Reviewer model
reviewer_model.description: Model for the first thorough review. Use inherit for the session model.

editor_model.title: Editor model
editor_model.description: Model for the agent that addresses findings. Use inherit for the session model.

verifier_model.title: Verifier model
verifier_model.description: Model for re-review passes that only verify prior findings.

model_routing.title: Model routing
model_routing.description: auto picks cheaper models where the work is mechanical: a small docs-only or config-only change with no risk probes gets a sonnet reviewer, a first editing round whose open findings are all minor and fence-backed gets a sonnet editor, and a finding reopened past the limit gets one strong arbitration pass before the run parks. fixed always uses the configured models.

review_samples.title: Review samples
review_samples.description: Independent reviewer passes per shard on the first review. Above 1, duplicates merge into the richest record with a support count the filter weighs; detection recall rises at roughly that multiple of the review cost. Reserve it for repositories where an escaped defect is expensive.

finding_filter.title: Precision filter
finding_filter.description: Before findings post, a cheap second context re-reads the cited code and demotes findings the fresh evidence cannot support into the round summary instead of inline threads. Nothing is dropped or closed; demoted findings are still addressed.

contract_commands.title: Contract command prefixes
contract_commands.description: Comma-separated command prefixes, beyond the check command itself, that a finding's Check line may start with to be executed during verification (example: go test, cargo test). Use test runners only, never bare interpreters. Empty means only the check command's own prefix runs.

cost_posture.title: Cost posture
cost_posture.description: Which way routing leans on each pull request where the change itself does not settle a decision. It never pins a model. economy counts more changes as small enough for the cheap reviewer (docs, config, or tests under 500 lines, no risk probe), fewer as large enough for the strong model (over 1200 lines of code), splits into shards over 2,250 changed lines, and starts any fix cheap once a check command gates the round. quality counts small under 150 lines and large over 400, splits over 1,000, starts only fixes with a proven suggestion cheap, and adds one review sample where a secrets, automation, or sensitive probe fired. balanced keeps 300, 800, and 1,500 and also starts fixes cheap whose Check line will execute. The reviewer also climbs for code whose changed files reference one another: 6, 4, or 2 couplings under economy, balanced, or quality. Reasoning effort reaches xhigh only under quality, and a signal that climbs the model does not also raise the effort. A blocker, a security finding, or a finding on a flagged file never starts cheap, and a fix that fails tries again one lever up whatever the posture. Fixed routing keeps every model and sample count as set; the shard limit and the effort cap still follow the posture.

sensitive_paths.title: Sensitive paths
sensitive_paths.description: Space-separated globs, relative to the repository, for files where a defect costs most (authentication, payments, migrations). A change touching one is treated like a change the sensitive probe flagged: the reviewer may climb to the strong model, no fix there starts on the cheap model, and the second review pass runs under the risky setting. A project's shared file adds to this list rather than replacing it.

migration_paths.title: Migration paths
migration_paths.description: Space-separated globs, relative to the repository, for database migration files; * also matches across directories. A change touching one is treated like a sensitive path, and the reviewer judges it for harm to databases and code other developers already run. Migrations are only ever read, never run. Your value replaces the default; a project's shared file adds to it.

strong_model.title: Strong model
strong_model.description: Model that auto routing climbs to for large code changes, for code whose changed files reference one another, for changes the probes flag as sensitive (concurrency, crypto, auth, injection surfaces), and that arbitration uses. Example: opus. Leave empty to cap routing at the reviewer model.
